Update `pysma` to version [0.5.0](https://github.com/kellerza/pysma/releases/tag/0.5.0). 
- List of sensors is now retrieved using a new method `sma.get_sensors()`
- Extra device classes (battery, energy meter) are now supported. (previously only inverter was supported)

issue_context.title: SMA Solar WebConnect sensors do not return any values
issue_context.body:
### The problem

Last working Home Assistant release: i try 2021.4.1 and 2021.4.6
Operating environment: Docker on Ubuntu 20.04
Component/platform: sensor/sma.py

After adding the required configuration for the SMA Solar WebConnect sensors, the sensors are created but do not return a value (all created sensors have Unknown as value).

In the homeassistant log i can see the message: 
```
**DEBUG (MainThread) [pysma] Sensor grid_power: No successful value decoded yet: {'65': [{'val': 423}]}**
```

The value in the log "423" i think its right, but what mean the full massage.

**Problem-relevant configuration.yaml entries:**
```yaml
sensor:
          - platform: sma
            host: SMA1901432067
            ssl: true
            verify_ssl: false
            group: user
            password: thePassword
            sensors:
                    - grid_power
logger:
  logs:
    default: info
    homeassistant.components.sensors.sma: debug
    pysma: debug
```
comments:
Hey there @kellerza, @rklomp, mind taking a look at this issue as its been labeled with an integration (`sma`) you are listed as a [codeowner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L432) for? Thanks!
<sub><sup>(message by CodeOwnersMention)</sup></sub>

The "65" key is unexpected.
In my case this is what is returned:
`{'1': [{'val': 55}]}`

What kind of device do you have? What software version is it running?

A custom sensor might work here to read the 65:

```yaml
custom:
  my_power:
   key: 6100_40263F00
   unit: W
   path: '"65"[0].val'
```

Hallo @rklomp, Hallo @kellerza,
thanks for your fast reaction :-)
I read from a "SMA ENERGY METER" with the Firewareversion 2.0.18.R, may be the version 2.x can makes problems.

I try the custom example, i does tests in the past with "custom" but without the path propertie. This works and i get the value now.

How familiar are you with developer tools in your browser?
Would you be able to provide me some extra information? Maybe we could improve the `pysma` library so no custom sensors are needed.

Login to the webinterface of your device and go to https://SMA1901432067/#/spotvalues
This should give you a page with all measurements of the device. If not, find that page in your GUI manually.

Open developer tools, go to network tab. Click clear in the top left and make sure recording is on. Then reload the page (F5).
You should now see a lot of requests. Save these requests as a HAR file and share that file.

This document might help:
https://support.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/204410413-Generating-a-HAR-file-for-troubleshooting

Thats sounds nice, thanks.
Here you are [sma1901432067.zip](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/files/6387179/sma1901432067.zip)

Thanks! Interesting to see every value is using 65 instead of 1. 
Can you create the recording including the refresh of the page? So I also have the javascript and json datafiles?

@kellerza 
We could add `'"65"[0].val'` as an extra JMESPATH_VAL_IDX?  
I am also trying to see if we can create a sensor mapping per device type, or a dynamic sensor generation

Now i record a second one, is it now more?
[sma1901432067_2.zip](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/files/6387615/sma1901432067_2.zip)

Thanks! Looking good.
Can you also make a recording of https://SMA1901432067/#/settings ? If I have that one as well I have a good overview of all paramaters your device type is providing.

Could you run the following command in your home assistant docker container? 
`pip install git+https://github.com/rklomp/pysma.git@patch-1`

This will install a patched pysma library. When installed you should be able to revert back to your original config as posted in your first post without getting any `No successful value decoded yet` errors.

Let me know it that works

Hallo @rklomp,
i have update the pysma with your command and rollback the custom settings.
The command provide me that the version is switched:
 ...
  Found existing installation: pysma 0.3.5 - Uninstalling 
  Successfully installed pysma-0.4.3

The pip show command shows me also the version 0.4.3.

But the parsing do not work and i see the message in the log again:  
  [pysma] Sensor grid_power: No successful value decoded yet: {'65': [{'val': 2977}]}

Hi @itinside 

Please try the latest dev version: `pip3 install git+https://github.com/kellerza/pysma.git`

Hi @rklomp,
i have do this but its the same: [pysma] Sensor grid_power: No successful value decoded yet: {'65': [{'val': 855}]}

Could you try running `example.py` from my `dev` branch against your Energy Meter?
https://github.com/rklomp/pysma/tree/dev

This should work and return correct values.
